back: Also called revolving credit; it allows repeated borrowing up to a credit limit.
No fixed number of payments; you can pay any amount above the minimum.
Credit cards are the most common example.
Sum the daily balances for the billing cycle, then divide by the number of days.
$$\text{Avg Daily Balance} = \frac{\text{Sum of Daily Balances}}{\text{Days in Billing Cycle}}$$
It includes purchases and payments as they occur.
cards.front: How is the [[kw:average daily balance]] calculated?
Calculate the average daily balance for a 30‑day month: $600 for 10 days, $400 for 20 days.

back: $$\text{Finance Charge} = \text{Average Daily Balance} \times \frac{\text{APR}}{12}$$
APR ÷ 12 gives the monthly periodic rate.
Example: Avg balance $800, APR 18% → monthly rate 1.5%, FC = $800 × 0.015 = $12.
cards.front: How do you find the monthly finance charge on a credit card?

back: Interest is calculated on the balance at the beginning of the billing cycle.
Payments made during the cycle are **not** subtracted before computing interest.
Results in the highest finance charge of the three methods.
Interest is computed on the beginning balance minus any payments made during the cycle.
Most favorable to consumers.
$$\text{Adjusted FC} = (\text{Previous Balance} - \text{Payments}) \times \text{Monthly Rate}$$
Previous balance method: $1,000 × 0.015 = $15.00.
Adjusted balance method: ($1,000 – $200) × 0.015 = $12.00.
Adjusted saves $3.00.
cards.front: Compare the finance charges: previous balance $1,000, payment $200, APR 18%.

back: The time (usually 21–25 days) after a billing cycle during which you can pay in full without interest.
Only applies if the previous balance was paid in full.
If you carry a balance, new purchases accrue interest immediately.
Pay the statement balance in full by the due date every month.
This preserves the grace period.
Cash advances usually have no grace period.
cards.front: How can you avoid all interest on a credit card?
What happens if you only make the [[kw:minimum payment]]?
back: Most of the payment covers interest; very little reduces principal.
The debt can linger for years and cost much more in total interest.
[[imp:Paying more than the minimum dramatically cuts payoff time.]]

cards.front: Calculate the new balance: previous $800, finance charge $12, purchases $100, payment $50.
back: The balance increased despite the payment.

cards.front: What is the blueprint for credit card finance charge problems?
back: 1. Understand: identify method, APR, previous balance, payments, purchases, cycle days.
2. Solve: compute average daily balance (or appropriate base), monthly rate, FC, and new balance.
3. Conclude: state FC and new balance; compare to previous balance.
